title: Hotpath memory leak in quantized serving causing degraded throughput and p99 crash loops
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency capacity event we observed a regression in quantized model serving where the continuous-batching hotpath leaked KV-cache-backed buffers and triggered p99 latency spikes and crash loops for a subset of models with mixed-precision attention. This ticket captures the incident follow-up, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and long-term action items to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Incident window ~2026-02-28 22:10 - 2026-03-01 03:45 UTC. Affected ~0.9% of hosted inference requests (peak) across three popular open models (llama-2-family variants) served with int8+kv-cache on G4/RTX clusters. Symptoms: sustained p99 latency increase up to 18s, a small but meaningful increase in token-level accuracy drift (~1.5% QA evals on internal prompts), several autoscaler-triggered instance restarts (crash loops), and failed canary rollouts. Customer-facing errors: 502/504 spikes; no data leak.
timeline: 2026-02-28 22:10 UTC: First alert from latency SLOs (p99 tails). 2026-02-28 22:18 UTC: Ops on-call increases logging and activates debug canary. 2026-02-28 23:05 UTC: Crash loops observed on 4/18 nodes running quantized serving binary v2.3.8. 2026-02-28 23:40 UTC: Emergency rollback to runtime-2.3.6 for affected pools reduces crash loops but p99 still elevated. 2026-03-01 01:10 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis narrowed to KV cache eviction path + a rounding-stability change in int8 dequant routine. 2026-03-01 02:30 UTC: Hotfix candidate built (PR #github/4228) and canaried on low-traffic pool; p99 restored. 2026-03-01 03:45 UTC: Incident declared mitigated.
root_cause: A regression introduced in runtime-2.3.8 changed the dequant rounding fallback in the int8 execution path to a faster vectorized code path. Under high concurrency, a race between the KV cache eviction thread and the new dequant buffer reuse logic allowed stale buffer slices to be reused while still being referenced by in-flight attention kernels. That produced two effects: occasional numerical perturbations (manifesting as small accuracy drift on sensitivity prompts), and transient corruptions that prompted out-of-bounds reads leading to worker process aborts (crash loops).
mitigation: Immediate actions: rolled back affected pools to runtime-2.3.6, disabled aggressive KV cache prefetching in the autoscaler for quantized pools, and limited concurrent batch sizes to reduce pressure on buffer reuse. Built and canaried hotfix patch that adds a borrow-check on dequant buffer lifecycle and restores deterministic rounding for the degraded code path (PR #github/4228).
action_items: A1: Add deterministic borrow/ref counting to dequant buffer pool and enforce single-writer guarantee (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate 5 pts, due 2026-03-16)
A2: Add end-to-end canary suite that runs mixed-precision attention microbenchmarks with concurrency SLOs for every runtime release (owner: Sofia Nguyen, estimate 3 pts, due 2026-03-20)
A3: Expand nightly regression evals to include priority customer prompt sets flagged as sensitivity tests to capture small accuracy drifts (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate 3 pts, due 2026-03-18)

A4: Instrument KV-cache eviction metrics (eviction latency, buffer reuse counts, borrow failures) and add alerting thresholds tied to p99 latency deviation (owner: Observability team, estimate 2 pts, due 2026-03-14)
A5: Update rollout playbook: for quantized-serving releases require a slow canary for 48h with autoscaler disabled for first 6h, then limited burst enabled (owner: SRE, estimate 1 pt, due 2026-03-13)
A6: Backport hotfix to runtime-2.3.x branch and schedule dedicated capacity pools to rotate through patched nodes (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate 2 pts, due 2026-03-12)
A7: Post-release audit: run a 24h synthetic workload that reproduces the original concurrency pattern and validate no buffer borrow races (owner: QA, estimate 2 pts, due 2026-03-22)
A8: Create a developer lint rule that warns when introducing fast-path dequant variants without explicit borrow semantics in PRs (owner: Compiler team, estimate 3 pts, due 2026-03-30)
A9: Document the behavioral trade-offs between deterministic rounding and performance across model families in the model-catalog (owner: Model Onboarding PM, estimate 2 pts, due 2026-04-05)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: No p99 latency increase > 20% over baseline in the 72h window after backporting hotfix on dedicated pools.
AC2: Canary suites include mixed-precision concurrent microbenchmarks and pass for 48h before a full rollout.
AC3: New metrics for buffer borrow failures and KV eviction latency are ingested and have alerts firing correctly in playbook tests.
AC4: Nightly regression evals detect accuracy drift >0.5% relative to baseline and open automated tickets for investigation.
comments: 2026-03-01 Marcus Lee: Began implementation of borrow-check on dequant buffer pool. Local stress tests reproduced race when concurrency > 48. Patch on branch fix/quant-borrow-check.
2026-03-02 Sofia Nguyen: Canary suite updated to include the customer prompt set; running 24h now against low-traffic pool; observed stable p99 after hotfix on canary nodes.
2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Nightly regression harness extended; added 3 sensitivity prompts that previously showed the 1.5% drift. Running side-by-side comparison scheduled every PR in the runtime repo.
2026-03-06 Observability Team: New metrics for eviction latency are live in prod; created dashboard with correlation to p99. Alert runbook updated.
2026-03-09 SRE: Deployed backport to dedicated pools for customers on reserved capacity. No crash loops reported in 72h.
2026-03-11 Marcus Lee: Submitted PR to add developer lint rule; needs review from compiler team and runtime maintainers.
2026-03-12 Product note: PMs informed and will update model-catalog docs; plan to communicate mitigations to impacted customers where appropriate.
